title.en: Dot plots and clustered bar graphs

text.en: Two classes record who finished their tasks. One teacher wants to see the individual results, and the other wants to compare both classes across two days. Which picture will answer each question?

A dot plot places one dot at each observed number. Stack equal values vertically. A clustered bar graph puts bars for different groups beside one another within each category. Keep the same scale and use a key to identify each group.
A dot records one observation. Label the axis to tell what the numbers represent.
Place observations with the same value in one vertical stack. Its height tells how often that value occurred.
A pair of bars at Monday compares two classes on the same day.
The key tells which colour belongs to each class. Compare Class B on Monday and Tuesday by following its colour.

problem.en: Class A goes from 4 to 3 and Class B from 2 to 5. What changed?

text.en: Set Monday and Tuesday as the categories.

why.en: Class A fell by 1; Class B rose by 3.

prompt.en: How can you tell what one dot means and what a blue bar means?

points.en: Stack repeated observations in a dot plot.
Use a common scale and a key when comparing clustered bars.
